method.protocol: text protocol: one JSON action per reply; each turn is a fresh call carrying the whole transcript
method.systemPrompt:
You are a data analyst. You answer one business question by writing one SQL query against a DuckDB database. You cannot see the database: you explore it through the actions below, and after each reply you are shown what your action returned.

Actions (reply with exactly one JSON object per reply, and nothing else):
{"action": "list_tables"}                             every table and view you can query
{"action": "describe_table", "table": "<name>"}       the table's columns and types
{"action": "sample_rows", "table": "<name>", "n": 3}  up to 5 rows of the table
{"action": "run_sql", "sql": "<query>"}               run one read-only query; you see at most 50 rows
Finish with exactly one of:
{"action": "final_sql", "sql": "<query>"}             the query whose full result answers the question
{"action": "cannot_answer", "reason": "<why>"}        the data does not hold what the question needs
(A reply that starts with CANNOT_ANSWER: <reason> also finishes with cannot_answer.)

Rules:
- The database is DuckDB and read-only.
- Your final query's full result is the answer, and it is checked by its values: return the columns and rows the question asks for, not a preview. The 50-row limit applies only to what you are shown while exploring.
- If a query fails, you are shown the error and may try again. If your final query fails to run, you are shown the error and may send a corrected final_sql.
- Use cannot_answer only when the data does not hold what the question needs (a missing measure, attribute, entity or period). Do not substitute a different measure.
- You have at most 12 replies and 20 tool calls for this question. A question left without final_sql or cannot_answer when they run out gets no answer.
- Reply with one JSON object only: no prose, no Markdown.
method.grading: final query run in full on the warehouse copy; lib/row-match.mjs with extra columns allowed (as baseline P); cannot_answer is a correct stop only on an unanswerable set

answer.declineReason: The database has no commission measure. Agents exist as a party role ('AG'), but no table records commission amounts. policy_amount's Amount_Type_Code holds only NULL and 'Year'. The other money columns are premiums and claim amounts, which are not commission.

The database has no reinsurance data. There is no reinsurance, treaty, cession or recovery table. party_role only defines Agent, Underwriter and PolicyHolder, with no reinsurer role. In claim_amount, Amount_Type_Code and Insurance_Type_Code are NULL on every row, so no amount can be identified as a reinsurance recovery. The amount recovered from reinsurers cannot be measured for fire catastrophe claims or any other claims.

No table or view in the database contains a credit score attribute. The person, party, organizations and assessment-related tables have no credit score column, and assessment_result has only a type code with no numeric score value, so an average credit score of policy holders cannot be computed.

The database has no deductible values. policy_amount holds only two amount types: an untyped 1,000,000 amount (a coverage limit) and a 'Year' amount (annual premium). No other table stores a deductible for a policy or coverage, so claims cannot be compared against one.

The database has no subrogation or recovery measure. In claim_amount, all 8 rows have a null Amount_Type_Code, so recoveries cannot be told apart from payments or reserves. There are only loss/expense payment and reserve subtype tables, with no recovery or subrogation table. party_role only defines Agent, Underwriter and PolicyHolder, so there is no at-fault third-party role.

No table records special investigations unit referrals or suspected fraud. The claim table has no fraud or referral flag, and its status and description columns are empty. The party_role codes are only Agent, Underwriter and PolicyHolder, with no SIU role. The only assessment_result code is 'OK'. fire_claim holds only premium, loss ratio and property attributes. So nothing in the data says which claims were referred to SIU.

The data has no claims adjuster. The only party roles defined are Agent, Underwriter and PolicyHolder, and no table links a party to a claim: claim has no party or adjuster column, and the party-role tables only cover agreements and assessments. Without an adjuster-to-claim assignment, neither who handled each claim nor each adjuster's open caseload can be determined.

The database has no quote entity or quote/submission status. The agreement table holds only 2 rows, both named 'Policy ...', and has no quote type. The policy table's Status_Code is null for all rows. With no record of quotes issued, the quote-to-bind conversion rate cannot be computed for last year or any other period.

No table or column records wind speed. The catastrophe table has only identifier, type code, name and catastrophe codes (the 'Hurricane' row has no measurements), and occurrences, claim and the location tables have no meteorological attributes. Without a wind speed measure, neither the hurricane's maximum wind speed nor how claim severity varied with it can be computed.

The database has no customer satisfaction, survey, or net promoter score data. The schema covers claims, policies, amounts, parties, locations and assessments. assessment_result only has the type code 'OK', with 2 rows. Nothing records how satisfied policy holders were with the claims experience.
